ai.description: This slender, cylindrical lizard reaches 15 cm. It is pale yellow or beige with a metallic sheen and possesses reduced, three-toed limbs adapted for sand-swimming. It lacks visible external ear openings.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophiomorus tridactylus* is uniquely distinguished by having only three digits on each limb, whereas most other similar Indian skinks possess four or five toes.
ai.habitat: *Ophiomorus tridactylus* inhabits arid, sandy desert regions of the Thar Desert, typically found in sparsely vegetated dunes or loose, sandy soils at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Indian sand-swimmer is primarily crepuscular, using its wedge-shaped snout to "swim" through loose desert sands to evade predators and hunt small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophiomorus tridactylus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–3 eggs. Breeding occurs during the summer months, generally between May and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ophiomorus tridactylus* is found in the arid, sandy desert regions of Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically occurring at low elevations within the Thar Desert ecosystem.
